extracted.intended_audience: aspiring sketch comedy writers / SNL writers / television comedy writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and selecting sketches for Saturday Night Live's weekly television show, including the week-long production schedule, cultural expectations in the writers' room, and the editorial rubric Lorne Michaels uses to choose sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lorne Michaels' Founding Credo
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let's make each other laugh, and if we do, we'll put it on television and maybe other people will find it funny."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical standard: primary litmus is whether the writers themselves find it funny; internal laughter is the first filter before considering audience appeal or production viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monday writers' meeting (kickoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers' meeting kicks off in Michaels's office. Day of redemption after Saturday's brood. Goal: make the host feel like one of the gang. Throw ideas around with cast and host.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production/process criterion: use Monday meeting to align on tone and host fit, generate collaborative ideas with cast and host, and set the week's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuesday night: high-volume independent drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Up literally all night writing sketches. Each writer drafts independently. High volume of sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production expectation: produce many distinct drafts overnight; quantity is prioritized to surface strong premises and jokes to be evaluated later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wednesday read-through selection
rubrics_metrics.description: All sketches read aloud. Cast and host laugh (or don't). Lorne picks the keepers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection mechanism: evaluate live read-through reaction (laughter, timing) as a key signal; Lorne's picks after the read-through determine what advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thursday–Friday rewrites and punch-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected sketches rewritten in writers' rooms. Punch ups, cuts, replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial process: focus on tightening, heightening, and excising weak material; expect iterative rewriting and replacement of weaker beats or jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturday dress rehearsal and final cuts
rubrics_metrics.description: Dress rehearsal at 8pm. Final cuts before 10:45 producers' meeting. Live show 11:30pm. Last cuts based on dress rehearsal performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final-evaluation checkpoint: use dress rehearsal audience/performer feedback and timing to make last-minute decisions; material may be cut/trimmed for length or punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal competition / rewrite-table culture
rubrics_metrics.description: The rewrite tables were rough; sketches torn apart sketch-by-sketch. High joke quota. Anonymous-feeling pitch process during rewrites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural expectation: be prepared for aggressive critique, a high demand for jokes per page, and an environment where ideas are scrutinized deeply and sometimes anonymously during the rewrite process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong premise (one unusual thing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a strong premise (one unusual thing)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core creative criterion: the sketch should hinge on a clear, singular unusual or surprising idea that differentiates it and drives the comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heightening across beats
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it heighten across beats? (Heightening structure / escalate the situation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural criterion: the sketch should build, escalate, or 'heighten' through successive beats so that stakes, absurdity, or comedic payoff increases rather than repeating the same gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct and quotable characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Are characters distinct and quotable? (Memorable character / quotable lines)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization standard: characters should be clearly differentiated, have recognizable traits or voices, and generate lines that audiences can remember and repeat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host showcase / star vehicle potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the host shine in this? (Star vehicle for the host)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting suitability: evaluate whether the sketch plays to the host's strengths, persona, or skills, increasing the likelihood of a standout performance and audience connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual or topical hook
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hook criterion: the sketch should offer a strong visual gag or timely topical angle that immediately grabs attention and differentiates it on television.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad audience appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it land with broad audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience-fit metric: consider whether the joke/premise will play to a national, late-night television audience (versus being too niche or insider), especially important for live broadcast reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch category fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketch Categories at SNL: cold open (often political); monologue (host's standup); recurring character sketches; one-off premise sketches; commercial parodies; game show parodies; music sketches; Weekend Update (news satire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre/format consideration: choose a category that suits the premise and host, and be aware that different categories have different conventions, pacing, and audience expectations which affect evaluation and editing.
